newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian 1996 steel output drops five percent.
newsitem.headline: Russian 1996 steel output drops five percent.

text.p: Russia's steel industry showed a five percent decline in production in 1996, with output falling to 49.2 million tonnes, the State Statistics Committee said on Tuesday.
The drop comes after a five percent increase in output in 1995 on 1994's level.
Steel pipe production in 1996 fell six percent to 3.5 million tonnes, after rising four percent in 1995 on the previous year. The committee gave no breakdown for products.
The decline mirrors a drop in Russian industrial output, which has halved since Moscow launched market-economy reforms in January 1992 and which contracted five percent in 1996.
Russia exports around 60 percent of its steel output and domestic consumption is about 17 million tonnes annually, according to the International Iron and Steel Institute.
Russia and the European Union extended a steel export agreement in December 1996 by six months while a new trade deal is hammered out.
